package_info.package_name: Coinbase.Core (and related: BinanceOfficial, Anarchy.Wrapper.Net, DiscordRichPresence.API, Avalon-Net-Core, Manage.Carasel.Net, Asip.Net.Core, Sys.Forms.26, Azetap.API, AvalonNetCore, Json.Manager.Core, Managed.Windows.Core, Nexzor.Graphical.Designer.Core, Azeta.API)
package_info.why_malicious: These packages impersonate legitimate libraries using typosquatting and misleading names, and contain or depend on a malicious init.ps1 script that executes arbitrary PowerShell code during installation or solution open. This script downloads and executes a second-stage payload (Impala Stealer) capable of credential and cryptocurrency wallet theft. The attack exploits NuGet's autorun script mechanism to achieve code execution without user interaction, resulting in data exfiltration and persistent compromise.

execution_context.trigger: install-time and solution open (via Visual Studio Package Manager Console)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At install-time and on solution open, the script sets the PowerShell execution policy to Unrestricted, downloads an executable from a hardcoded external IP over HTTP, saves it to the user's AppData directory, and executes it, resulting in remote code execution and delivery of a second-stage payload.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The script disables PowerShell execution restrictions, downloads and executes an untrusted binary from the internet automatically during package installation or solution open, and does so without user consent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate NuGet packages should not execute code on install, modify execution policies, or download and run external binaries. Use of init.ps1 for such actions is highly abnormal and dangerous.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: In rare cases, enterprise packages may use init.ps1 for environment setup, but never to download and execute remote binaries or alter execution policies.
key_indicators: Sets PowerShell execution policy to Unrestricted
Downloads executable from hardcoded external IP address
Runs on install and every solution open
No user interaction or consent required
Presence of init.ps1 in tools directory

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At install-time, when the main package is installed, a dependency package containing the malicious init.ps1 script executes, setting the PowerShell execution policy to Unrestricted, downloading an executable from a remote server, saving it to the user's AppData directory, and executing it, resulting in remote code execution via the dependency chain.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Malicious code is concealed within a dependency, making detection more difficult and increasing the attack surface. The script performs the same dangerous actions as in the root package.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate dependencies should not contain autorun scripts that execute arbitrary code, especially not scripts that download and run external binaries.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Chained dependencies are common, but using them to execute code or download binaries is not legitimate.
key_indicators: Malicious payload hidden in dependency package
Same download-and-execute pattern as root package

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
Binary payload (Impala Stealer):
- Steals crypto wallets (e.g., Exodus Lightning wallet)
- Exfiltrates data via Discord webhooks
- Extracts and executes code from Electron archives
- Drops updater to C:\Users\user\AppData\Local\Squirrel-2021\Updater.exe
- Connects to C2 for updates
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the downloaded binary searches for cryptocurrency wallet data and credentials, exfiltrates stolen data via Discord webhooks, extracts and executes code from Electron application archives, and installs a persistent updater in the Squirrel-2021 directory to maintain access and receive updates.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The binary performs credential and wallet theft, uses Discord webhooks for data exfiltration, extracts code from Electron archives, and establishes persistence via a dropped updater, all of which are hallmarks of stealer malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No legitimate package should install or run a binary that steals credentials, exfiltrates data, or establishes persistence as part of its installation or runtime behavior.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: There are no legitimate use cases for these behaviors in standard NuGet packages.
key_indicators: References to crypto wallets and Discord webhooks
Drops persistent updater in Squirrel-2021 directory
Electron archive extraction and code execution
Steals and exfiltrates sensitive user data

init.ps1 script executes automatically, sets PowerShell execution policy to Unrestricted.
attack_chain.leads_to: Download and execution of second-stage payload

attack_chain.action: init.ps1 downloads Impala.exe from remote server and executes it.
attack_chain.leads_to: Second-stage payload runs on victim machine

attack_chain.action: Impala.exe (second-stage payload) steals credentials and crypto wallets, exfiltrates data, and establishes persistence.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to sensitive data and maintains control

behavioral_signatures: Presence of init.ps1, install.ps1, or uninstall.ps1 in NuGet package tools directory
init.ps1 scripts that set PowerShell execution policy to Unrestricted
init.ps1 scripts that download and execute binaries from external sources
Automatic execution of PowerShell scripts on install or solution open
init.ps1 scripts referencing hardcoded external IP addresses or URLs
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan NuGet packages for the presence of init.ps1, install.ps1, or uninstall.ps1 scripts in the tools directory. Flag any scripts that set PowerShell execution policy to Unrestricted, download files from external sources, or execute downloaded binaries. Monitor for network connections to known C2 IPs and Discord webhooks. Watch for creation or execution of suspicious binaries in %APPDATA% or Squirrel-2021 directories. Use package metadata analysis to detect typosquatting and impersonation attempts. Correlate behavioral and file indicators to reduce false positives and prioritize packages exhibiting multiple suspicious characteristics.
